knowledge-base.name: pr-review
knowledge-base.triggers: PR review, code review, pull request, feedback, LGTM, approve, request changes
knowledge-base.overview: Code review serves knowledge transfer, maintaining code health, and creating historical records. Approve code that improves overall health, even if not perfect.
knowledge-base.rag-requirement:
Before writing any finding or starting any review pass, run these three calls in order: 1. rag_context(agent="reviewer-agent", task_description="code review [description]", max_tokens=4000) 2. rag_search(scope="codebase", project_path=[repo], query="[one-sentence summary of what changed]", limit=5) 3. rag_search(scope="codebase", project_path=[repo], query="[same summary]", limit=5, mode="graph")
Why this is mandatory: RAG surfaces existing patterns (guards, projections, conventions) before any code is reviewed. Reviewing a diff in isolation means pattern-inconsistency bugs won't be caught. In ASC-1201, an IsNotNullOrEmpty guard existed on DiagnosisIds but was missing on the new fields. RAG would have surfaced the pattern immediately. It was only caught in QA.

core-principles.principle: Approve code that definitely improves overall code health, even if not perfect
Effectiveness drops beyond 400 lines of code

category.name: Functionality
category.check: Verify code solves the stated problem
Check for logic errors: off-by-one, incorrect conditionals
Examine edge cases: empty, null, boundary, min/max
Verify error handling with meaningful messages
Review test coverage for edge cases and error paths

category.name: Code Quality
category.check: Functions should be small and focused
Flag code with >3-4 levels of nesting
Flag excessive branching (long if/else chains)
Variable/function/class names clear and descriptive
Comments explain WHY, not WHAT
Remove commented-out code
Replace magic numbers with named constants

category.name: SOLID Principles
category.red-flag: Classes mixing business logic with persistence/presentation/logging
Long if/else chains checking types, frequent instanceof
"Fat" interfaces where clients implement unused functionality
Direct dependencies on concrete classes, liberal use of new

category.name: Input Validation (OWASP Top 10)
category.check: SQL injection: Use parameterized queries
Command injection: Handle safely
Path traversal: Validate file paths
All user inputs: Validate, sanitize, escape

category.name: Auth
category.check: Robust authentication mechanisms
Proper session handling with timeouts
Password storage: bcrypt or Argon2
Authorization checks at all entry points
CSRF protection

category.name: Data Exposure
category.check: No passwords/tokens/credentials in code or logs
Error messages don't expose system details
Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit

performance-review.check: Flag O(n²) or worse without justification
Check for N+1 query problem (queries in loops)
Verify appropriate indexes for WHERE and JOIN
Large result sets: use pagination or streaming

golden-rules.rule: Comment on the code, never on the developer
Avoid condescending words: just, easy, only, obvious, simply

actionable-feedback.good: The calculateTotal function lacks error handling for invalid input. Please add checks for negative numbers.

clear-framework.step: Mentally execute with sample data, test boundaries

two-pass.pass: Detailed line-by-line, edge cases, error handling

timing.rule: Respond within one business day maximum

self-review-checklist.description: Trigger-conditional review passes. Read the diff FIRST, evaluate each trigger, then run only the passes whose triggers fire. Skipped passes must appear in output as "N/A: [reason]" — proving they were considered, not forgotten.

pass.name: Simplicity
pass.trigger: Always runs — applies to every PR.
pass.check: Can this be deleted, inlined, or simplified? What's the smallest version that still works?
Question any regex, string manipulation, or multi-step encoding.
Is there a simpler way in this framework?

pass.name: Already-Exists
pass.trigger: Fires when: new utility, helper, component, or abstraction is introduced.
pass.skip-when: Only modified existing code — no new abstractions added.
pass.check: Does the codebase or a dependency already provide this?
Search for similar utilities/components/hooks/services before keeping your version.
But verify the existing thing actually meets the requirement — reusing a single-select widget for a multi-select requirement is worse than creating a new one.

pass.name: Dead Code
pass.trigger: Fires when: code is deleted, parameters are added, or functions are introduced.
pass.skip-when: Pure additions with no removals or new params.
pass.check: For every variable/param/function: is this actually referenced? Trace it end-to-end.
For every CSS class: is this used in the HTML?
For every param: does the caller ever pass anything other than the default?

pass.name: Debug Cleanup
pass.trigger: Always runs — debug artifacts can appear in any change.
pass.check: Search for: console.log, alert(), commented-out code, hardcoded test data.
Check click handlers: is this for real functionality or was it for testing?
Any temporary logs, toasts, flags, debug UI left behind?

pass.name: Convention Compliance
pass.trigger: Fires when: new elements are added to an existing page, file, or module.
pass.skip-when: Greenfield new file with no sibling elements to compare against.
pass.check: For EACH new element: identify the nearest sibling elements that existed before this PR.
List every attribute/pattern those siblings use (e.g., disabled, readonly, CSS classes, data attributes, event handlers, guard conditions).
Verify the new element follows ALL of them — not just the ones that affect functionality.
Specific to Profile.cshtml: enableProfileEditing, isCRMControlledField, validation spans, CSS classes, .Enable() on Kendo widgets, disabled/readonly on HTML elements.
Specific to any page with permission guards: every new interactive element must respect the page's edit/read-only contract.
pass.incident-reference: ASC-1171: Four Kendo MultiSelects correctly used .Enable(enableProfileEditing) but two plain HTML elements (select, input) were missing disabled/readonly guards. The pattern was on every other field on the page. Caught by bot reviewer, not by human or agent review.

pass.name: Common-Pattern Breaker
pass.trigger: Fires when: a new pattern is introduced that differs from how the codebase usually solves this problem.
pass.skip-when: Following an existing pattern exactly — no deviation.
pass.check: Am I breaking a shared convention or introducing a one-off pattern?
If deviating: add a short comment in the PR description explaining why, what alternatives were considered, and what to watch for.

pass.name: Fresh Eyes
pass.trigger: Always runs — applies to every PR.
pass.check: Read every line like you didn't write it: why does this exist? What would I delete first?
Would a senior reviewer question this? If yes, simplify it now.

pass.name: Ticket Alignment
pass.trigger: Always runs — every PR should implement exactly what was asked.
pass.check: Re-read the ticket after coding.
Check acceptance criteria one by one.
Remove scope creep, "while I'm here" improvements, and speculative features.

pass.name: Spec Precision
pass.trigger: Fires when: UI copy, labels, field names, statuses, or error messages are added or changed.
pass.skip-when: Backend-only changes with no user-facing text.
pass.check: UI copy matches spec exactly (e.g., "ticket saved" != "Ticket Saved").
Field names, labels, statuses, and error messages match the spec.
Behavior matches described states and edge cases precisely.
If the ticket says "multi select" — verify the widget actually allows selecting multiple values.
If the ticket says "alphabetical" — read the list top to bottom and confirm A-Z order.

pass.name: Manual Smoke Test
pass.trigger: Fires when: UI changes, JS widget changes, or user-facing interactions are modified.
pass.skip-when: Backend-only changes with no UI impact.
pass.check: For each AC scenario, physically perform the described action — don't trust code reading alone.
Kendo/JS widgets can behave differently than the HTML suggests — click it to verify.
If you can't run it locally, flag that explicitly.

pass.name: Migration/Schema
pass.trigger: Fires when: model properties are added, removed, or changed.
pass.skip-when: No model/entity changes in the diff.
pass.check: Every model property add/remove MUST have a matching migration.
Run dotnet ef migrations add and verify the generated migration does what you expect.
Check the snapshot file matches your model.

approve-when.criterion: Code definitely improves overall code health
Functionality correct and edge cases handled

request-changes-when.criterion: Functionality incorrect or missing critical edge cases

context.focus: Full review: architecture, security, performance, testing
Maintains behavior, improves quality, adequate tests
Request split, or walkthrough, multiple sessions

process.bad: Provide all feedback in one pass

communication.bad: Excessive nitpicking on trivial style issues
